method.name: gdpp_create
method.description: Creates an instance of the class's scene, like [code]create[/code] in GD++ code, and returns its root. The scene is loaded once, by the first call. Returns [code]null[/code] if the scene fails to load, or if its root isn't an object of this class, so always check the result. [code]new()[/code] creates the node alone, without the scene.

method.name: gdpp_destroy
method.description: Frees the object right away, like [code]destroy[/code] in GD++ code. It's thread-safe: on other threads than the main one, it leaves nodes in the scene tree to the main thread, which frees them at the end of the frame.

method.name: gdpp_queue_destroy
method.description: Frees the node at the end of the frame, like [code]queue_destroy[/code] in GD++ code, and [method Node.queue_free].

method.name: gdpp_scene_cache
method.description: Loads the class's scene and keeps it, so that [method gdpp_create] doesn't load it later, e.g. when a level loads. Does nothing if the scene is kept already. Prints an error if it fails to load. It's thread-safe.

method.name: gdpp_scene_evict
method.description: Drops the class's kept scene, e.g. when a level is unloaded, so that Godot can free it once nothing else uses it. The next [method gdpp_create] or [method gdpp_scene_cache] loads it again. Objects created from it stay as they are. It's thread-safe.
